newsitem.title: USA: Vencor launches Transitional Hospital offer.
newsitem.headline: Vencor launches Transitional Hospital offer.

text.p: Vencor Inc., a diversified provider of health care services, said Wednesday it has begun a cash tender offer to acquire competitor Transitional Hospitals Corp. for $639 million, topping a rival bid for the company.
Vencor's $16-a-share bid tops a bid of $14.55 a share by Select Medical Corp., which was announced earlier this week.

The combination of Vencor and Transitional, which operates long-term acute care hospitals, would advance the growth strategy of Vencor, the nation's largest full-service long-term healthcare provider, Vencor said in a statement.

The combined company would have 57 hospitals, 314 skilled nursing centres, 4,000 institutional customers for contract rehabilitation services, 80,000 employees and pro forma annual revenues of $3.3 billion. Vencor said it would retain all of Transitional's non-administrative employees, but did not say how many people might be laid off.

Vencor said it is filing a lawsuit in U.S. District Court in Nevada to invalidate a $19.4 million termination fee called for in the merger agreement between Transitional and Select and will raise its bid by two-thirds of the amount by which the termination fee is reduced if it is successful.

The Vencor offer is scheduled to expire June 4, 1997, and is subject to at least two-thirds of Transitional's fully diluted common shares and equivalents being tendered. The offer has no financing contingency.
